preamble: Twelve clues lead to solutions that are longer than their allotted slots in the grid. Adjustments of a consistent sort must be made to each of these solutions to produce a real word (with the length indicated in the letter count after its clue) that will fit the grid. Two of the 12 original solutions are two words.

clue.text: He shouldn't be working in second vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle for hire

explanation.surface: Someone off sick or unlicensed is caught driving a second car when they should be resting.
explanation.walkthrough: A scab is a strike-breaker: during a strike he should not be at work, which is why the definition reads as a moral judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a worker who crosses a picket line, so during a strike he is the one who ought not to be working.

clue.text: Not for visiting Byzantium

indicators.note: a visitor is briefly inside a place, so the answer sits inside the letters of the city's name

parts.note: the four letters sit in the middle of the city's name, straddling its Z

explanation.surface: A traveller declines a trip to the ancient city of Byzantium.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti is a preposition meaning opposed to, the opposite of being in favour of something.

clue.text: Cause to bring goods into German city

indicators.note: to bring goods into a city is to carry them inside it, so the goods letters go within the city's name
into says where the goods end up: within the city's letters

parts.note: Trier is a city on the Moselle in western Germany
G is short for good, so goods is two of them

explanation.surface: A trader is given a reason to ship merchandise into a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: GG for goods is a crossword convention: G stands for good, doubled for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, which is the verb sense of cause.

clue.text: More than one plane tree pest is unfortunately covering

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover, or wrap round, the tree
something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of pest is are disturbed

parts.note: these six letters are the raw material to be rearranged
a fir is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: Plane trees are being smothered by some pest, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes plane a tree (the London plane); in the answer it is an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a British fighter aircraft of the Second World War, so the plural is several such warplanes.

clue.text: Greenery is prone to be occupied by London coppers and sappers

indicators.note: a house occupied by tenants holds them, so the coppers and sappers go inside the lying-down word

parts.note: to lie is to be prone, flat on the ground
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: A park's foliage keeps being trampled by police and army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds LIME TREES, one of the two two-word solutions; a run of letters is then cut to fit the five-letter slot, leaving LIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime trees, the lindens of avenues and parks, are leafy greenery; in the grid they shrink to limes, the same trees by another name.

clue.text: It helps breathing, being cool and well rested, initially

parts.note: in means fashionable, the slang sense of cool
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of rested only

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Keeping calm and getting a good night's sleep makes breathing easier.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler is a device asthmatics use to take medicine into the lungs, making breathing easier.

clue.text: Abusive rascal interrupting Hindu's address, endlessly base person

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so the rascal sits within the Hindu title

parts.note: Sri is an Indian honorific placed before a name
a cur is a worthless scoundrel

indicators.note: the last letter of the base person is cut off

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A scoundrel barges into a holy man's speech and turns out to be a thoroughly low type.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurrilous language is coarse and insulting, the sense of abusive used of remarks.

clue.text: Can protection for frolicking be this?

definitions.text: Can protection for frolicking be this?

indicators.note: letters that frolic are cavorting about, so can protection is rearranged

parts.note: these thirteen letters are the raw material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: could a rubber be just the thing for a romp?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives CONTRACEPTION, which the whole clue also describes; two letters come out to fit eleven squares, leaving CONTRAPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraception is protection against pregnancy during sex, which the clue coyly calls frolicking.

clue.text: Queen, say, losing right heel

indicators.note: losing means the letter for right drops out

parts.note: a queen is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A monarch, perhaps, breaks the right heel of her shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen looks royal, but here it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a man who behaves dishonourably, and cad is a dated synonym for such a rotter.

clue.text: Days suffering without drink, having trouble with consumption

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the jumbled letters sit outside the drink
the letters of days are in a bad way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters are the raw material to be rearranged
Pepsi is a brand of cola

explanation.surface: Someone goes days unwell without a drop to drink, unable to keep food down.
explanation.walkthrough: Without is the old sense of outside, not lacking; consumption is eating, not tuberculosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, a disorder of the stomach after eating.

clue.text: Putting logo on bottom of badminton racket — boast about it

indicators.note: the boasting word goes about, or round, the other letters

parts.note: to brag is to boast

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written across is its last letter

parts.note: its last letter supplies the piece
din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: A sponsor's badge goes on a badminton racket, and the player shows off about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket is noise here, not the bat. The wordplay makes BRANDING; three letters are cut to fit the slot, leaving BRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Branding is the marketing practice of stamping a product with a company's mark, which is putting a logo on it.

clue.text: Tailless bird circles character in Old Testament book

indicators.note: the shortened bird goes round the biblical name
the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a thrush is a songbird
Esau is Jacob's twin brother in Genesis

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail is described as circling a figure in a book of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Testament book looks like the definition, but book alone is; the Old Testament supplies the character.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference work listing synonyms, so it is a kind of book.

clue.text: A family name's brought back still

parts.note: taken as written
kin are your relatives

indicators.note: brought back means the naming word is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A family's old surname is revived, yet things stay the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Name is a verb here (to cite), not a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Akinetic is the technical term for lacking movement, so it means motionless.

clue.text: Girl with an apple for cooking, getting dressing

indicators.note: cooking letters mixes them up, so girl, an and apple are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman brings a cooking apple and ends up with salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing suggests the kitchen, but it is clothing. The anagram gives APPARELLING; two letters are cut, leaving APPALLING.
explanation.definitionFit: To apparel someone is to clothe them, so the participle names the act of putting clothes on.

clue.text: Gliding and tripping in chilled party in Africa in Gabon's capital

parts.note: iced means cooled, as with a drink
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress party
taken as written

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of Gabon

parts.note: the country's name supplies just its initial

explanation.surface: A dancer skates and stumbles at a cool party held in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripping is dancing nimbly, as in tripping the light fantastic, not falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice dancing is the figure-skating discipline where couples glide and perform dance steps on the ice.

clue.text: Record company not about to enter Home Counties for a short interval

indicators.note: the label and the turned word go in between the letters for the Home Counties

parts.note: the counties around London, in the South East of England
EMI is a British record label

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so not is read backwards

parts.note: the three letters of not are taken and turned round

explanation.surface: A record label briefly moves its offices into the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds SEMITONE; two letters come out, leaving SEMITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest step in Western music, the gap between adjacent piano keys, so it is a short musical interval.

clue.text: Secretary to mock and criticise hard lines

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
to rag is to tease
to rap is to rebuke sharply

explanation.surface: A secretary teases a colleague and tells them 'hard lines', meaning tough luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard lines is a British idiom for bad luck, which hides that lines is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragraph is a block of several lines of text forming one unit of writing.

clue.text: Diver's parking before one leaves

parts.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking

indicators.note: one, as the letter I, leaves the word for before

parts.note: earlier means before in time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A diver's car is parked just before someone leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives PEARLER; three letters come out, leaving PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearler is someone who dives for pearl oysters, a pearl diver.

clue.text: Frenchman sent back rules for overhaul

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

indicators.note: sent back means the word for rules is reversed

parts.note: law is a body of rules

explanation.surface: A Frenchman returns the regulations so they can be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds RENEWAL; two letters are cut, leaving RENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal of something is a thorough restoration of it, which is what an overhaul is.

clue.text: Con coins from US academics

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
cents are the small coins of American money

explanation.surface: American professors are cheated out of their money.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay makes DOCENTS; three letters come out, leaving DOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a docent is a university teacher below professor rank, so docents are academics.

clue.text: Animal painter not quite right, entering just like a mule

indicators.note: the painter's name stops one letter short

parts.note: George Stubbs was an 18th-century English painter of horses

indicators.note: the right goes into the word for just

parts.note: only means just, as in just one

explanation.surface: A painter of animals, not quite on the mark, paints a mule exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds STUBBORNLY; three letters are cut, leaving STUBBLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are proverbially obstinate, so behaving stubbornly is acting like one.

clue.text: Colour's very loud in most of Asian dress with no back

indicators.note: the loud mark goes inside the shortened dress
most of the dress means all but its final letter
the back, or last letter, of the dress is missing

parts.note: a sarong is a wrapped skirt worn in South-East Asia
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A garish colour clashes loudly on a backless Asian dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is the deep orange-yellow shade of the spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Deliberately fencing a cabin

indicators.note: fencing round means enclosing, so the a goes inside

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone builds a fence round a hut on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliberately is used in its sense of unhurried, which is how lento is played.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, a small hut much like a cabin.

clue.text: Graduate bets capital from east Asian land

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
to lay a bet is to place it

indicators.note: read from the east, that is from right to left, the letters are reversed

parts.note: A1, here written AI, means first-rate or capital

explanation.surface: A graduate stakes money in a capital city somewhere in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital is the old adjective for excellent, A1, written with the letter I for the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaysia is a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Small animals retreating in flight

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: pets are animals kept at home

explanation.surface: Little creatures run away in panic.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight suggests escape, chiming with retreating; here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of stairs between landings, a series of steps.

clue.text: Current trainee returned schedule for hospital device

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
a cub is a novice, as in cub reporter

indicators.note: returned means read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: A trainee on the wards hands back the electricity rota for a piece of medical equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Current is not electricity here but fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubator is the heated enclosure in which premature babies are kept in hospital.

clue.text: Collapse cooking kale and tofu

indicators.note: cooking ingredients alters them, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegan dinner of kale and tofu falls apart in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives FLAKE OUT, one of the two two-word solutions; three letters come out, leaving FLOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To flake out is an informal phrase for collapsing from exhaustion or falling asleep.

clue.text: Supervisor finished date with queen

parts.note: a match that has finished is said to be done and ended
to see someone is to date them
R for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A boss ends a romance in order to take up with a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds OVERSEER; four letters are cut, leaving OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer is a person who watches over and directs workers, a supervisor.

clue.text: Hint and sign in eastern puzzle

parts.note: a faint trace of flavour, a hint
the ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A clue and a symbol are hidden in a puzzle from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds TANGRAM; three letters come out, leaving TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is the Chinese dissection puzzle of seven flat shapes rearranged into figures.

clue.text: Low-down fellow? Not quite

indicators.note: the word for fellow stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a gent is a man, short for gentleman

explanation.surface: A rather base man is not entirely a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Low-down looks like an adjective for a rotter, but it is the noun for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Gen is British slang for information, the same meaning as the low-down on something.

clue.text: Something in the blood, cheek or toe fixed with pin

parts.note: lip is impudence, as in don't give me any lip

indicators.note: fixed means repaired, so the letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An injury to the face or foot is mended with a surgical pin.
explanation.walkthrough: Something in the blood sounds like inherited character; here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipoprotein is a compound of fat and protein that carries cholesterol through the bloodstream.
